result.summary: This wide urban intersection features high-visibility crosswalks with green conflict zone markings and dedicated pedestrian signals. However, the significant crossing distance across multiple travel lanes increases pedestrian exposure and risk from turning vehicles.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians are exposed to multiple lanes of traffic for a long duration due to the width of the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, spanning the width of the intersection.

hazards.name: High-Speed Turning Potential
hazards.description: The wide intersection geometry and lack of curb extensions may encourage vehicles to make turns at higher speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Right corner near the pedestrian crossing.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to provide a safe waiting area and allow pedestrians to cross the wide street in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The image depicts a multi-lane urban intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and a dedicated green-painted bike lane. While the infrastructure is modern and well-maintained, the wide crossing distance across multiple travel lanes increases pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross three travel lanes and a bike lane without a mid-point refuge, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk spanning the width of the roadway.

hazards.name: Multi-lane one-way traffic
hazards.description: The one-way, multi-lane configuration can encourage higher vehicle speeds and creates multiple threat scenarios for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: If space permits, install a raised refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

result.summary: The image shows a dense urban environment with wide sidewalks, a marked crosswalk, and a dedicated bike lane. Pedestrian infrastructure includes curb ramps with tactile warnings and street lighting, though the multi-lane roadway presents some exposure risk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb may block the sight lines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, ahead of the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers by moving the waiting area into the line of sight.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines for all road users.
